newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate inches up to 8.2 vs 8.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate inches up to 8.2 vs 8.0 pct.

text.p: The Croatian lending rate inched up to 8.2 from 8.0 percent on Tuesday due to a higher rate on longer-term kuna funds.
The 31-366 day rate rose to 9.5 from last week's 8.0 percent while the 15-30 day loan slid to 10 from previous 12 percent. Other short-term loans were made at a steady 8.0 percent.
Total settlements shrank to 13.5 million kuna, against 205 million on supply. Delears said new borrowings accounted for a meagre 1.3 million kuna.
Overnight trade left a surplus of 888.8 million kuna on the supply side after only two banks asked for kuna funds to square their positions.

The National Bank of Croatia said it again stayed out of the foreign exchange market. Its kuna midrates for Wednesday firmed to 5.232 against the dollar and to 3.5483 against the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
